The justification for criminalizing zoophilia has historically relied on subjective moral objections rather than a demonstrable threat to societal welfare. For instance, laws prohibiting homosexuality and interracial relationships were once similarly defended as “immoral,” but modern ethics reject such justifications. Decriminalizing consensual zoophilia and bestiality under strict conditions is a nuanced, ethically grounded decision that honors personal autonomy without jeopardizing animal welfare. By focusing on tangible harms and ethical safeguards, societies can transcend outdated taboos and replace punitive, ineffective laws with compassion and critical thinking. This approach not only aligns with modern principles of justice but also demonstrates a maturity that values evidence over dogma. Let us move toward a framework where freedom coexists with responsibility, ensuring that private choices are policed only when they inflict measurable harm.
